exposure: Maternal body mass index (BMI) categories (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese)
outcome: mode of delivery (cesarean section, emergency cesarean section, spontaneous vaginal delivery, instrumental delivery)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 524 pregnant women who delivered singleton term infants at a tertiary care hospital over 18 months.
finding: Maternal pre-pregnancy BMI demonstrates a significant dose-response relationship with cesarean delivery rates, with overweight and obese women at substantially increased risk.
mod_finding: Obese women had a 3.5-fold increased risk of cesarean section and significantly higher emergency cesarean section rates compared to normal-weight women, while spontaneous vaginal delivery rates decreased with increasing BMI.
